data.long_meaning: Jagatkar is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'jagat' meaning 'world' and 'kar' meaning 'doer'. It is believed that the name refers to the supreme god who is the creator and sustainer of the universe. Jagatkar is a revered name in Hinduism and is given to boys as a mark of respect and devotion. The name Jagatkar carries the meaning “Lord of the Universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jagatkar usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Jagatkar dynasty ruled over the princely state of Jaisalmer from 1350 to 1639 AD. The Rajput rulers of this dynasty were known as the Jaisalmers or Rawals of Jaisalmer.

The name 'Jagatkar' is derived from the Sanskrit term 'Jagat', meaning 'world' and 'Kar', meaning 'doer' or 'ruler'. This name was commonly used by the Rajput rulers of the Jaisalmer region to signify their role as the rulers of the world (Jagat) in the medieval period of India.
